title: sync-agenda-innovation-roadmap-prep-zoe-2026-03
content:
Purpose / meeting intent:
- Prep for 1:1 sync w/ Eng (Marco) + Applied ML (Priya) to align on the experimental lane for Q2: low-latency lightweight models for ephemeral chat flows.
- Outcome: agree on 3 concrete experiments, owners, and minimal data/metrics we need to start canary.

When:
- Friday 2026-03-13, 10:00-10:45am PT (block = 45m).

Who (expected):
- Zoe Patel (PM, hosting product) - lead agenda
- Marco Chen (Eng, serving-runtime) - feasibility + infra cost
- Priya Kapoor (Applied ML) - model/quantization tradeoffs
- Liam Rivera (SRE / Observability) - dashboarding and SLIs (optional)

Topline framing (one sentence):
- We need a short runway to validate if a quantized 7B variant + prefix KV cache can meet 150ms p50 for short-turn chat with <30% quality regression versus full fp16 model, at <=40% token cost.

Agenda (rough):
1) Quick sync on goal & constraints (5m)
   - remind: target product flows (support micro-interactions, search suggestion).
2) Present baseline metrics we have (8m)
   - what we measure: cold p50/p95, warm p50/p95, token cost, top-1 accuracy proxy (BLEU-ish / eval set), regen rate from UX telemetry.
3) Priya: experimental model options + expected perf/cost tradeoffs (8m)
   - quantization approaches (4-bit, GPTQ, QLoRA?), cache friendliness, KV size implications.
4) Marco: infra constraints and rollout plan (8m)
   - GPU pool vs dedicated pods, batching implications, autoscale triggers, fallback to hosted full model.
5) Decision: pick top 3 experiments and owners (8m)
6) Instrumentation & observability plan (6m)
7) Action items, next steps, cadence (2m)

Prep notes / what I will bring:
- Small eval set (30 prompts) representing short-turn chat; current baseline numbers (p50/p95 warm/cold) from last week.
- UX telemetry summary: regen rate + sample qualitative failures.
- Cost estimates for hosted fp16 13B and fp16 7B (per-1M tokens).

Key open questions to resolve in meeting:
- Q1: What is an acceptable quality delta? (product leaning: <=20% measurable drop on eval set; Priya caution: metric mismatch)
- Q2: How aggressive can infra be on batching w/o breaking 150ms p50 target? (Marco to estimate)
- Q3: Can we get gated rollout (canary per-customer) with current console features or do we need a quick flag in the serving runtime?
- Q4: Do we need a small human eval window before canary to validate hallucination/regressions?

Expected decisions (draft):
- Experiment A: FP16 7B, baseline caching + modest batching (owner: Marco)
- Experiment B: 4-bit quantized 7B using GPTQ-style pipeline, no extra batching initially (owner: Priya)
- Experiment C: Hybrid flow - fp16 13B for complex prompts, fast-track 7B for conditional short prompts (owner: Zoe)
- Toggle decision: we will use feature-flag rollout via Dedicated routing if available; else use region-routing fallback.

Minimal instrumentation for canary (must-have):
- Latency p50/p95 (cold and warm)
- Token cost per request (estimate + realtime)
- Quality proxy on eval set (automated re-run daily)
- Regen/drop rate from UX telemetry
- Error / fallback counts

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Bring concrete numbers for baseline: last run (2026-03-06) shows warm p50 for 13B = 210ms, warm p95 420ms, cost ~ $0.012/token-equivalent (?) -> double-check with finance calc sheet.
- Need to check if the console rollout supports per-model canary; if not, escalate to platform eng.
- If Priya recommends Q4 quantization path, confirm memory layout & KV cache compatibility.

Potential risks (brief):
- Quality regression not captured by proxy metrics -> require quick human sample.
- Autoscale oscillation when traffic mixed (short-turn vs long-turn).
- Increased tail latency during cold starts for quantized models.

Follow-up actions (populate during/after meeting):
- [ ] Marco: estimate batching latency curve (p50 vs batch size) + cost delta by 2026-03-20 (owner: Marco Chen)
- [ ] Priya: run small GPTQ-ish pipeline on eval set and report quality delta & mem footprint by 2026-03-18 (owner: Priya Kapoor)
- [ ] Liam: create dashboard template (latency, regen rate, cost) and share link by 2026-03-17 (owner: Liam Rivera)
- [ ] Zoe: draft canary rollout doc + acceptance criteria and circulate for review by 2026-03-15 (owner: Zoe Patel)
- [ ] Zoe/Marco: check console feature for per-customer routing flags and log results in linked_artifacts by 2026-03-14 (owners: Zoe, Marco)

Parking lot (not for this meeting):
- Explore per-request dynamic routing (cost-aware) for mixed flows.
- Investigate dedicated tiny-model pool for ephemerals.

Post-meeting quick template I will paste in follow-up slack: (keep short)
"Thanks all — captured decisions: A/B/C selected, owners assigned. Next steps: Marco to share batching curve, Priya to share GPTQ run, Liam to prod dashboard, Zoe to write canary doc. Target check-in: 2026-03-20. I'll post the meeting notes + action items to #prod-hosted-api and link Confluence."

Personal reflection (notes to self after run of this prep flow):
- Keep the eval set small but representative; prioritize real UX failure modes over synthetic metrics.
- Push for one measurable acceptance criterion (e.g., regen rate delta <= 5%) in addition to p50 latency target — helps product decide quickly.
- If infra says batching kills p50, consider microservice path: precompute responses for ultra-short flows (hacky but short-term win).

End of scratchpad.
